name: DDB
description: DDB returns the depreciation of an asset for a specified period using the declining balance method, typically double the straight-line rate.
tldr: Calculates double-declining balance depreciation for a specified period.

parameters.name: salvage
parameters.description: Value at the end of the depreciation life.

parameters.name: life
parameters.description: Number of periods over which the asset is depreciated.

parameters.name: period
parameters.description: The period for which to calculate depreciation.

parameters.name: factor
parameters.description: Rate at which the balance declines (default 2 for double-declining).

basicExample.explanation: A $10,000 asset with 5-year life depreciates $4,000 in the first year using double-declining balance.

advancedExamples.title: Custom declining factor
advancedExamples.description: Use a factor of 1.5 for 150% declining balance
advancedExamples.explanation: Factor 1.5 produces a slower decline than the default factor of 2.

howItWorks: DDB applies a fixed rate multiplied by the factor to the remaining book value. The default factor of 2 creates double-declining balance. The method does not switch to straight-line automatically.

howToSteps.name: Calculate
howToSteps.text: Press Enter to get the result.

limitations: Total depreciation may exceed salvage value if not monitored.
Does not switch to straight-line automatically like VDB.
Factor can be changed for different depreciation speeds.

commonErrors.cause: Period is invalid or cost < salvage.
commonErrors.fix: Check that period is between 1 and life and cost >= salvage.

commonErrors.cause: DDB does not stop at salvage value automatically.
commonErrors.fix: Use VDB or manually limit the final period.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: DDB works identically in Google Sheets.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Same syntax and behavior as Excel.

faq.question: What is the default factor for DDB?
Can DDB switch to straight-line?
faq.answer: No, use VDB for a method that switches to straight-line.
